thread:
elena: quick question — for backports that are telemetry-only (no customer-facing behavior), should we: 1) bump patch (v1.4.2 -> v1.4.3), or 2) keep the same patch and append build metadata (v1.4.2+ci.202403), or 3) no tag change and only ship a release note?

sam: my instinct is patch bump. keeps pins simple.

rajesh: patch bump + clear release note. buildmeta sucks for pinning because many package managers ignore it.

morgan: +1. Also: can we avoid creating a bunch of noise releases for telemetry-only churn? we have a few of those every week.

elena: that’s the tradeoff. ops wants deterministic pins for Dedicated customers, but product folks hate tiny micro-releases for nonfunctional changes.

rajesh: idea: classify changes as "nonfunctional-deps" vs "functional". For nonfunctional-deps we do a patch bump but mark release notes `chore: telemetry-only` and tag the commit with `v1.4.3-telemetry.1`?

sam: meh — introducing extra pre-release suffixes complicates consumers. many downstream scripts expect semver core only.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: CI artifact created for commit abc123: image=redwood/inference:1.4.2+ci.4578, tag=ci/3123579. Canary window open.

elena: seeing the above — deploy-bot and CI can keep buildmeta for internal artifacts, but canonical git tags that we publish for customers should be semver core (X.Y.Z) only. that way pins are clear.

morgan: so rule proposal: 
- internal CI artifacts: include build metadata (`+ci.<buildnum>`)
- public release tags pushed to repo: only bump patch for any backport that touches production code, including telemetry-only.
- if the change is pure docs or release-note-only, do not bump.

sam: +1 on that. also add: group telemetry-only backports into a single weekly patch when possible to reduce release churn.

rajesh: corner case: if a backport touches a translation file or localization that some customers rely on, we should treat as functional. i.e., patch bump always unless strictly docs.

elena: agreed. i’ll draft a one-paragraph policy for the release playbook: keep canonical tags simple (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), CI can use buildmeta, and batch telemetry/nonfunctional backports when ops latency allows.

morgan: also add an explicit rollback play: if a patched release needs rollback, we prefer tagging a follow-up patch (v1.4.4) that reverts, not unpublishing tags. avoids surprises for pinned Dedicated envs.

sam: +1 — never unpublish tags for semver stability.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary for v1.4.3 scheduled 2024-03-29 22:00 UTC; notify #oncall on completion.

elena: thanks — will update release notes template to include `type: nonfunctional` and a short justification. will post PR to docs.

morgan: perfect. that should keep both product and ops happy.
